# The anatomy — the shape every generated workflow takes

One house shape, so any two forge workflows read as the same system. Sections in
this order, always. A section that does not apply is omitted, never reordered.

```yaml
# >>> press:gha-header … GENERATED by @natjswenson/press, do not edit
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  NS ┃ CI · NODE TEST                          linkedin.com/in/natejswenson
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#  Lint and test on every pull request into main.
#  generated by forge 0.1.0 — regenerate, do not hand-edit
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# <<< press:gha-header
name: CI                       # 1. the display name, matching the masthead eyebrow

on:                            # 2. triggers — narrowest set that does the job
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:           #    almost always: one line, and re-runs stop needing fake commits

permissions:                   # 3. ALWAYS present, deny-all floor
  contents: read

concurrency:                   # 4. one in-flight run per ref
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  test:                        # 5. job id: lowercase, hyphenated, names the check
    name: test                 #    this string becomes the `ci / test` context
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15        # 6. NEVER omit — the default is 360
    permissions:               # 7. job-level when fewer than all jobs need it
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha>   # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false   # 8. unless this job actually pushes
      # setup → install → verify, in that order, one concern per step
```

## Why each is load-bearing

**`permissions:` always, explicitly.** Repos created before 2023 still default
`GITHUB_TOKEN` to read/write on nearly everything, so a compromised transitive
dependency in a test run gets a repo-write token. And the block is *exhaustive*
once written — anything unlisted becomes `none`, which is the number-one cause of
"it worked until we added permissions". Grant at the **job** level whenever fewer
than all jobs need it; job-level replaces workflow-level, it does not merge.

**`timeout-minutes:` always.** The default job timeout is **360 minutes**. One
deadlocked test costs six billed hours before Actions notices.

**`concurrency:` always.** Without it, five pushes in a minute is five full billed
runs, and anything touching shared state races. Two shapes that differ on purpose:

| Case | group | cancel-in-progress |
|---|---|---|
| PR / CI | `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` | `true` |
| Deploy / publish / Pages | a literal name (`pages`, `npm-publish`) | **`false`** |

Cancelling a half-finished deploy leaves the target indeterminate. Never cancel a
publish.

**`persist-credentials: false` on checkout** unless the job pushes. Checkout
writes a live token into `.git/config` and leaves it there for the whole job; any
later artifact upload of the workspace publishes it as a downloadable file.

**Every `uses:` pinned to a full 40-char SHA with a `# vX` trailing comment.**
The comment is not decoration — it is the only place the readable version
survives, and `forge verify` reads it to report staleness.

## Naming

| Thing | Convention | Why |
|---|---|---|
| file | `ci.yml`, `release.yml`, `pages.yml` | lowercase, one word where possible |
| `name:` | `CI`, `Release`, `Deploy Pages` | title case; becomes the masthead eyebrow |
| job id | `test`, `build`, `publish` | lowercase-hyphenated |
| job `name:` | matches the id unless a matrix needs interpolation | **this string is the required-check context — renaming it silently un-requires the check** |
| step `name:` | omitted when the `run:` is self-evident | a name that restates the command is noise |

## The masthead

Never hand-written. `forge header <file> --purpose "…"` splices it; the brand
lives in `press/brand/tokens.json` and nowhere else. `forge check` re-derives it
and fails on drift, absence, or a stale press version.
